name: Joe's Stone Crab
description: The most famous restaurant in Miami, period. Been here since 1913. No reservations — you wait in line like everyone else, or hit the takeout window like a local.
must_try: Stone crab claws with mustard sauce and a side of key lime pie

name: Versailles Restaurant
description: The beating heart of Cuban Miami. Politicians, abuelitas, and tourists all end up here. The mirrored dining room is a landmark. Open breakfast through late night.
must_try: Vaca frita with black beans and maduros, then a cafecito at the ventanita

name: Cote Miami
description: Michelin-starred Korean steakhouse in the Design District. The Butcher's Feast is the move — dry-aged cuts grilled tableside. One of the best restaurants in the country.

name: The Surf Club Restaurant by Thomas Keller
description: Thomas Keller's Florida outpost inside the restored Four Seasons Surf Club. Michelin-starred Continental classics. The room alone is worth the trip.
must_try: Whole roasted Dover sole, soufflé for dessert

name: Zucca
description: Beloved Italian in Coral Gables' Hotel St. Michel. Michelin-trained chef, 2,000 bottle wine cellar. The veal parm and stuffed zucchini flowers are outstanding.

name: Tâm Tâm
description: Started as a pandemic pop-up, now one of the best restaurants in Miami. Creative Vietnamese in a quirky downtown diner space. There's karaoke in the bathroom.
must_try: Tam Tam wings in fish sauce caramel

name: Sunkissed
description: Brickell's sexy new supper club. Red monochromatic room, live band every night, Miami-influenced seafood. The arroz con pollo is a sleeper hit.
must_try: Arroz con pollo, live music on a Wednesday date night

name: Casa MX
description: The Mexican spot Miami needed. Incredible huitlacoche quesadillas, smoky salsa with free chips, and carnitas tacos that'll ruin Taco Tuesday for you forever.

name: Klaw
description: Three-story surf-and-turf showstopper in Edgewater's historic Women's Club building. The ambiance is gorgeous and the food delivers.
must_try: Whole grilled fish, raw bar plateau

name: Caracas Bakery
description: Venezuelan bakery with some of the best pastries in Miami. The ham cachito and chocolatine croissant are legendary. Line moves fast.

name: Gramps Getaway
description: Dock-and-dine spot at Rickenbacker Marina with killer downtown skyline views. Elevated bar food — the conch fritters and charred broccoli salad are both great.
must_try: Conch fritters, charred broccoli salad with pickled chili

name: Rusty Pelican
description: Possibly the best skyline view of any restaurant in Miami. Seafood-forward, great brunch with bottomless mimosas. Book at sunset.
must_try: Brunch with bottomless mimosas, sunset dinner on the patio

name: El Palacio de los Jugos
description: Open-air cafeteria where you point at what you want. Roast pork, fresh juices, whole fried snapper. No English needed. This is real Miami.
must_try: Roast pork with yuca, fresh mamey milkshake

name: Gianni's at the Former Versace Mansion
description: Dine inside the Versace Mansion. The Italian food is solid, the setting is unreal — mosaic pool, gold everywhere. Pure Miami excess.
must_try: Dinner on the patio by the famous pool

name: Seaspice
address: 422 NW N River Dr, Miami, FL 33128
description: The Miami River scene restaurant. Pull up by boat, dress up, be seen. Mediterranean seafood and scene-y vibes. Weekend brunch is pure spectacle.

name: Komodo
description: Three-story Southeast Asian restaurant in Brickell. Part restaurant, part scene. The rooftop lounge transitions into nightlife after 10pm.

name: Cotoletta
description: One-dish restaurant concept in the Design District: a perfect Milanese veal cutlet with rosemary and lemon. That's it. That's the whole menu. It works.
must_try: The cotoletta. There's only one thing to order.

name: Smith & Wollensky
description: Classic steakhouse right at the tip of South Pointe with views of Government Cut and Fisher Island. The outdoor terrace is a sunset destination.
must_try: Bone-in ribeye, sunset on the terrace

name: Los Fuegos by Francis Mallmann
description: Francis Mallmann's live-fire Argentine steakhouse at the Faena. The parrilla is the show. One of the most romantic restaurants in Miami.

name: Tropezón
description: Spanish tapas on Española Way. Paellas, patatas bravas, gambas — all designed for sharing. Moorish tiles, tiny tables, and house-infused gins behind the bar.
must_try: Gambas al ajillo, any paella, infused gin cocktail

name: Robert Is Here
description: Legendary roadside fruit stand since 1959. Exotic fruit milkshakes, petting zoo, Grandma's Kitchen general store. Worth the drive south.
must_try: Key lime milkshake, mamey sapote milkshake

name: LIV
description: The most famous nightclub in Miami, inside the Fontainebleau. Global DJ residencies, celebrity sightings, bottle service spectacle. This is the 'I did Miami' checkmark.
must_try: Table service if you can swing it — the bottle parade is the show

name: E11EVEN Miami
description: The 24/7 ultraclub. #1 club in the US. Downtown Miami's unhinged, never-closing spectacle — live performers, DJs, rooftop restaurant, five-star excess at 4am.
must_try: Go at 3am on a Saturday when the energy peaks

name: Club Space
description: The last standing temple of Miami's house/techno scene. Warehouse energy, rooftop terrace for sunrise sets, the real dance-music-heads club. Across the street from E11EVEN.
must_try: Sunday morning terrace set — you'll understand when the sun comes up

name: STORY
description: LIV's sister club on Collins. Same team, same production quality, different vibe. World-class sound system, top-tier DJs. Dress sharp.
must_try: Check who's playing — the lineup is always stacked

name: Ball & Chain
description: Little Havana institution since 1935. Live salsa, Latin jazz, Salsero Sundays. The mojitos are strong, the dance floor is sweaty, and nobody cares if you can't salsa.
must_try: Salsero Sundays on the outdoor Pineapple Stage

name: Sweet Liberty
description: National award-winning cocktail bar. Feels like your cool friend's living room — amazing drinks, no pretension. One of the best bars in America.
must_try: Ask the bartender to make you something based on your mood

name: The Broken Shaker
address: 2727 Indian Creek Dr, Miami Beach, FL 33140
description: Craft cocktail pioneer at the Freehand hostel. Poolside drinks in a garden setting. The cocktails here literally changed the Miami bar scene.
must_try: Seasonal cocktail menu, anything with tropical fruit

name: Sugar at EAST Miami
description: Brickell's standout rooftop bar. Asian-inspired cocktails in an outdoor garden setting with panoramic bay and skyline views. Gets packed after 9pm.
must_try: Arrive at sunset for the view, stay for the cocktails

name: Mango's Tropical Cafe
description: The Ocean Drive spectacle. Live salsa dancers, thumping Latin music, neon lights. Touristy? Yes. A blast? Also yes. You'll dance whether you planned to or not.
must_try: Piña colada in a pineapple, watch the show from the patio

name: Mac's Club Deuce
description: The best dive bar in Miami Beach. Opened in 1964 and hasn't changed. Cheap drinks, pool table, zero attitude. Where locals go after their shift at the fancy places.
must_try: Cheap beer at 2am when the rest of the Beach is $20 cocktails

name: Blackbird Ordinary
description: Brickell's favorite bar. Giant backyard patio, strong drinks, DJs most nights. The place where everyone ends up at some point during a Miami night out.
must_try: Happy hour on the patio, then stay for the DJ

name: No. 3 Social
description: Wynwood rooftop bar with great views and a low-key vibe. Drag bingo Sundays. Solid happy hour daily 4-7pm. The place to start a Wynwood night.
must_try: Drag bingo Sunday, happy hour any day

name: Cerveceria La Tropical
description: Cuban beer brand reborn in Wynwood. Massive outdoor space, live music, Cuban food menu. The original Tropical lager recipe dates back to 1888 Havana.
must_try: Original Tropical Lager, Cuban sandwich, live music on weekends

name: Twist South Beach
description: Miami's most iconic LGBTQ+ nightlife venue for 25+ years. No cover, multiple rooms, dancing every night. A SoBe institution.
must_try: Drag shows and dance floor Saturdays

name: Jolene Soundroom
description: Truly underground — a historic Roaring Twenties basement turned open dance space on Flagler. Groovy house and techno. The real heads know this one.
must_try: Late night weekend set in the basement

name: Panther Coffee
description: Miami's homegrown specialty roaster. The Wynwood flagship is the original. Great pour-overs, cold brew on tap, good people-watching.
must_try: Cold brew on nitro, seasonal single-origin pour-over

name: Azucar Ice Cream Company
description: Abuela Approved ice cream in Little Havana. Cuban-inspired flavors. The 'Abuela Maria' (guava, cream cheese, maria crackers) is the signature.

name: Wynwood Walls
description: The outdoor museum that put Wynwood on the map. World-famous street art murals by Shepard Fairey, Os Gêmeos, and dozens of international artists.
must_try: Free street art in the surrounding blocks is just as good

name: Pérez Art Museum Miami (PAMM)
description: Waterfront contemporary art museum designed by Herzog & de Meuron. The building itself is as impressive as the collection. Great Bay views from the terrace.
must_try: The hanging gardens, terrace bay views, rotating exhibitions

name: Vizcaya Museum and Gardens
description: Italian Renaissance villa built 1914-1922 on Biscayne Bay. 10 acres of formal gardens, ornate rooms, waterfront views. Miami's most beautiful estate.
must_try: The formal gardens and bay-facing terrace at golden hour

name: ICA Miami (Institute of Contemporary Art)
description: Free contemporary art museum in the Design District. Currently hosting the Dolce & Gabbana exhibition through June 2026 — 300+ archival pieces.
must_try: Dolce & Gabbana exhibition (through June 2026), sculpture garden

name: Phillip and Patricia Frost Museum of Science
description: Top-tier science museum with a 3-story aquarium, planetarium, and rooftop with bay views. The Gulf Stream aquarium tank is mesmerizing.
must_try: The full-height aquarium, planetarium laser show

name: Art Deco Historic District
address: Ocean Drive and Collins Ave, Miami Beach, FL 33139
description: The pastel-colored Art Deco buildings of South Beach are iconic. Walk Ocean Drive and Collins between 5th and 15th Streets. Free self-guided, or join a walking tour.
must_try: Miami Design Preservation League walking tour ($30)

name: Adrienne Arsht Center for the Performing Arts
description: Miami's premier performing arts center. Broadway shows, Miami City Ballet, concerts, jazz. The building itself is stunning architecture on Biscayne Bay.
must_try: Check the calendar — the programming is always strong

name: Jungle Island
description: Eco-adventure park on Watson Island with ziplines, animal encounters, and Joia Beach (a private beach with cocktails and dining).
must_try: Joia Beach for cocktails, zipline through the canopy

name: Zoo Miami
description: The only tropical zoo in the continental US. 750 acres, 500+ species. The Amazon & Beyond and Florida exhibits are highlights.
must_try: The splash playground for kids, feeding giraffes

name: South Beach
address: Ocean Dr to the Atlantic, Miami Beach, FL 33139
description: The iconic beach. White sand, turquoise water, lifeguard towers in candy colors. The Lummus Park stretch is the classic scene.
must_try: Early morning walk before the crowds, sunset from South Pointe

name: South Pointe Park
description: 17-acre park at the very southern tip of Miami Beach. Watch cruise ships glide through Government Cut. Best sunset spot on the Beach.
must_try: Watch the cruise ships depart at sunset

name: Crandon Park Beach
description: Key Biscayne's family beach. Calmer water, coconut palms, less scene than South Beach. Consistently rated one of the best beaches in America.
must_try: The sandbar at low tide, kayak rentals

name: Oleta River State Park
address: 3400 NE 163rd St, North Miami Beach, FL 33160
description: Largest urban park in Florida — 1,043 acres on Biscayne Bay. Mountain bike trails, kayaking, secluded beach. A true escape inside the city.
must_try: Kayak through the mangrove tunnels, mountain biking

name: Biscayne National Park
description: 95% underwater national park. Snorkeling, glass-bottom boat tours, island camping. Home to the northernmost coral reef in the US.
must_try: Snorkeling at the reef, boat tour to Boca Chita Key

name: Everglades National Park
description: The River of Grass. Airboat tours, alligator spotting, mangrove kayaking. One of the most unique ecosystems in the world, 45 min from downtown.
must_try: Airboat tour, Anhinga Trail boardwalk for guaranteed gator sightings

name: Fairchild Tropical Botanic Garden
address: 10901 Old Cutler Rd, Coral Gables, FL 33156
description: 83-acre tropical garden on Biscayne Bay. Rare palms, tropical fruit, butterfly garden, mangrove preserve. Founded by the man who introduced avocados to America.
must_try: Walk all the way to the bay — mangrove forest is stunning

name: Bayside Marketplace
description: Waterfront shopping/entertainment complex on Biscayne Bay. Touristy but the bay views are free and it's the departure point for most boat tours.
must_try: Skip the shopping, take a bay cruise departing from here

name: Lincoln Road Mall
description: Miami Beach's pedestrian promenade. Mix of chains and boutiques, great people-watching, Sunday farmer's market. The social runway of SoBe.
must_try: Sunday farmer's market, outdoor dining and people-watching

name: Miami Design District
description: Open-air luxury shopping district. Gucci, Louis Vuitton, Dior — plus world-class galleries and restaurants. The architecture alone is worth the walk.
must_try: Window shop the luxury brands, eat at Cote or Cotoletta

name: Dolphin Mall
description: Miami's big outlet mall. Over 240 stores — Nike, Coach, Saks OFF 5TH. Not glamorous, but the deals are real.
must_try: Hit it on a weekday to avoid crowds

name: Fontainebleau Miami Beach
description: The iconic Miami Beach resort. Home to LIV nightclub, multiple pools, Hakkasan restaurant. Mid-Beach location. This IS the Miami resort experience.
must_try: Pool scene on a Saturday, LIV nightclub, brunch at Scarpetta

name: Faena Hotel Miami Beach
description: Miami's most artistic luxury hotel. Damien Hirst gold mammoth in the lobby, Baz Luhrmann-designed theater, Los Fuegos restaurant. Truly one-of-a-kind.
must_try: The living room lobby, Los Fuegos dinner, Faena Theater show

name: 1 Hotel South Beach
description: Eco-luxury resort on South Beach. Sustainable design, rooftop pool and bar, beachfront. The rooftop has some of the best ocean views in Miami.
must_try: Rooftop pool and bar at sunset

name: Freehand Miami
address: 2727 Indian Creek Dr, Miami Beach, FL 33140
description: Boutique hostel-hotel hybrid. Home to The Broken Shaker bar. The pool area is the social hub. Best budget-to-cool ratio on the Beach.
must_try: Broken Shaker cocktails by the pool

name: Publix Super Markets
description: Florida's beloved grocery chain. The sub shop (Pub Sub) is legendary. Get a chicken tender sub on sale day and you'll understand.

name: CVS Pharmacy
address: Multiple locations including 1421 Alton Rd, Miami Beach
description: Multiple 24-hour locations across Miami and the Beach. Your sunscreen-and-hangover-cure stop.

name: Thriller Miami Speedboat Adventures
description: High-speed boat tour of Biscayne Bay. Celebrity homes, Star Island, Fisher Island. Gets your adrenaline going and gives you the Miami skyline from the water.
must_try: The 45-min speedboat tour past Star Island

name: Island Queen Cruises
description: The classic Millionaire's Row Biscayne Bay cruise. Narrated tour past celebrity homes, Fisher Island, the Port of Miami. Tourist staple for a reason.
must_try: Sunset cruise — the skyline lights up as you come back

name: Elcielo Miami
description: Michelin-starred sensory journey through Colombian cuisine. Prepare for theatrical tableside presentations, including washing your hands in chocolate.
must_try: The Tree of Life bread presentation

name: Hiden
description: Ultra-exclusive eight-seat omakase counter hidden behind a taco stand. Michelin-starred. Book months in advance.

name: Le Jardinier Miami
description: Vegetable-forward Michelin-starred haven below L'Atelier. The outdoor patio is a stunning, lush oasis.

name: Stubborn Seed
description: Top Chef winner Jeremy Ford's Michelin-starred laboratory. Hyper-seasonal, beautifully plated American cuisine.

name: Ariete
description: Michelin-starred dining where homestyle Cuban cooking meets contemporary French technique. The tableside pressed duck is legendary.

name: Boia De
description: Tiny Michelin-starred Italian-ish gem hidden in a retro shopping plaza marked only by a neon exclamation point.

name: EntreNos
description: Michelin-starred champion of Florida sourcing. Almost everything on the menu comes from within the state.

name: Los Félix
description: Michelin-starred Mexican cuisine honoring ancestral traditions. Heirloom corn tortillas and an incredible natural wine list.

name: Ogawa
description: Intimate Michelin-starred omakase in Little River featuring seafood flown directly from Toyosu Market.

name: Shingo
description: Exquisite 14-seat omakase counter inside the historic La Palma building. Michelin star well-deserved.

name: Tambourine Room by Tristan Brandt
description: Ultra-exclusive 18-seat tasting menu experience tucked inside the Carillon Miami Wellness Resort.

name: Bachour
description: Gorgeous bakery and restaurant from world-renowned pastry chef Antonio Bachour. The petit gateaux look like modern art.

name: Chug's Diner
description: Cuban-American diner from Chef Michael Beltran that earned a Bib Gourmand. The cast-iron pancake is legendary.
must_try: Cast Iron Pancake and Cast Frita

name: El Turco
description: Authentic home-style Turkish food recognized with a Bib Gourmand. The meze platters are perfect for sharing.

name: Ghee Indian Kitchen
description: Farm-to-table Indian cuisine with produce grown on the chef's own Homestead farm. A true Miami culinary gem.

name: Hometown Barbecue Miami
description: The Brooklyn BBQ giant brings massive, beautifully smoked meats to an industrial space in Allapattah.

name: La Natural
description: Chic, minimalist spot famous for naturally leavened pizzas and a stellar selection of natural wines.

name: Lucali
description: Miami outpost of the legendary Brooklyn pizzeria, serving massive, perfectly charred pies in Sunset Harbour.

name: Mandolin Aegean Bistro
description: Stunning open-air Greek and Turkish restaurant in a restored 1940s home. A local favorite for breezy, romantic dinners.

name: Michael's Genuine Food & Drink
description: The restaurant that pioneered the Design District dining scene. Stellar farm-to-table American fare.

name: Phuc Yea
description: Loud, fun, fiercely original Viet-Cajun mashup wrapped in a 90s hip-hop soundtrack.

name: Sanguich de Miami
description: Cozy, bohemian Cuban coffee shop recognized by Michelin for outstanding pressed sandwiches and croquetas.

name: Cafe La Trova
description: James Beard award-winning chef Michelle Bernstein and cantinero Julio Cabrera created this retro-Cuban masterpiece with live music.

name: Enriqueta's Sandwich Shop
description: The best ham croquetas in Miami. Period. Cash-only counter-service institution in Wynwood.

name: Sunny's Steakhouse
description: What started as a pop-up is now one of the hottest steakhouses in the country, featuring a grand outdoor courtyard.

name: Carbone Vino
description: Intimate, extremely tough-to-book Italian from Major Food Group with a 3,000-bottle wine collection.

name: Time Out Market Miami
description: Heavily curated food hall featuring outposts from some of the city's best chefs under one roof.

name: Julia & Henry's
description: Multi-level culinary and entertainment destination breathing fresh life into historic Downtown Miami.
must_try: Natural wine at the central bar

name: Baires Grill
description: Stylish Argentinean steakhouse beloved by locals for prime cuts, empanadas, and excellent wine list.

name: Pisco y Nazca
description: Vibrant modern Peruvian eatery delivering bold ceviches and excellent pisco sours.

name: Schnebly Redland's Winery
description: Southernmost winery in the US, turning tropical fruits like lychee and avocado into wine, with a farm-to-table restaurant.

name: Chef Creole Seasoned Kitchen
description: Miami institution blending Haitian, Creole, and Bahamian flavors under a thatched-roof outdoor patio.

name: Seia
description: Breathtaking 2026 opening on the 54th floor with museum-quality art and extraordinary contemporary Italian cuisine.

name: Gramps
description: Fiercely independent Wynwood staple featuring great pizza, excellent cocktails, live music, and air conditioning.

name: J Wakefield Brewing
description: Star Wars-themed brewery famous worldwide for intense, heavily fruited Florida Weisse beers and massive stouts.

name: Veza Sur Brewing Co.
description: Vibrant Latin-inspired craft brewery serving highly drinkable lagers and beer cocktails in a lush outdoor setting.

name: Palace Bar & Restaurant
description: The legendary drag bar of Ocean Drive. Weekend brunch features queens literally stopping traffic to perform.

name: Tequila Town
description: Massive 25,000 sq-foot immersive exhibition taking guests on a multi-sensory journey through agave cultivation. Opening spring 2026.

name: Superhuman Museum
description: Opening late 2026, massive experiential art museum in the old Regal Cinema, focusing on art that inspires human potential.

name: Everglades Alligator Farm
description: One of the oldest alligator farms in South Florida, offering thrilling airboat rides and massive gator feeding shows.

name: Grotto Baths Wynwood
description: Miami's first modern social bathhouse opening summer 2026. 7,500 sq ft circuit of saunas, steam, and mineral pools. Alcohol-free.

name: The Surf Club Spa
description: Light-drenched sanctuary inside the Four Seasons with ocean views and clinical European skincare treatments.

name: Lapis Spa at Fontainebleau
description: Massive theatrical spa famous for elaborate water journeys including mineral pools and rain tunnels.

name: The Setai
description: Oasis of extreme Asian-inspired tranquility right in the middle of South Beach. The service is utterly flawless.

name: EAST Miami
description: Sleek, design-forward hotel anchored in Brickell City Centre with four pools and the famous Sugar rooftop bar.

name: Bal Harbour Shops
description: Most productive luxury shopping center in the world. Open-air enclave of koi ponds, tropical foliage, and high-fashion.

name: Brickell City Centre
description: Hyper-modern multi-level outdoor mall anchoring Brickell, famous for its massive Climate Ribbon canopy.
must_try: Browsing before dinner at Casa Tua Cucina

name: Lucky Strike Miami
description: Upscale boutique bowling alley with 28 lanes, dynamic arcade, and craft cocktails.

name: Reward Fishing Fleet
description: Miami's premier party boat fishing fleet from Miami Beach Marina. Perfect for casual anglers wanting affordable offshore experience.

name: All Day
description: Incredibly chic, award-winning coffee bar offering meticulous pour-overs and fantastic breakfast fare.

name: Zak the Baker
description: Legendary Kosher bakery and cafe turning out Miami's best sourdough, pastries, and incredible breakfast platters.

name: Floyd
description: Connected to Club Space and modeled after the Red Room from Twin Peaks. Luscious red velvet, quality sound, house and techno acts.

name: Do Not Sit on the Furniture
description: Intimate, underground-feeling electronic music venue on South Beach. Deep house and melodic techno in a dark, sweaty room. The antithesis of VIP culture.

name: Basement Miami Beach
description: Underground club beneath the Edition hotel with a bowling alley and ice skating rink. Unique multi-level layout. More accessible than LIV.
must_try: Bowl a frame then hit the dance floor

name: Hoy Como Ayer
description: Little Havana's other Latin music institution. More local, more raw than Ball & Chain. Live bands, strong drinks, real salsa.

name: El Patio Wynwood
description: Wynwood's reggaeton headquarters. Fridays are legendary. Open-air patio with Latin DJs pumping until late.

name: Cosanostra
description: High-energy Latin nightlife on Calle Ocho. Reggaetón, salsa, bachata, dembow. Festival-level atmosphere every weekend.

name: Employees Only Miami
description: The NYC speakeasy transplant. Hidden behind a psychic's neon sign. Impeccable classic cocktails and late-night dining.
must_try: The Amelia cocktail, late-night bone marrow

name: Better Days
description: Underground speakeasy beneath Sweet Caroline's in Brickell. Japanese whisky focus, dim lighting, meticulous cocktails.

name: Lagniappe
description: Wine bar and live music venue with a huge tree-shaded garden. Jazz, folk, and soul acts nightly. Bring your own cheese and they'll plate it.
must_try: BYOB cheese board with their wine, live jazz on a weeknight

name: Tipsy Flamingo
description: Playful, neon-lit cocktail bar on Lincoln Road. Giant frozen cocktails, Instagrammable decor, and a fun vibe.

name: The Regent Cocktail Club
description: Intimate, velvet-draped cocktail lounge inside the Gale Hotel. Art Deco glamour, live jazz, and meticulous classic cocktails.
must_try: The Hemingway Daiquiri, live jazz Friday

name: Wynwood Brewing Company
description: Wynwood's first craft brewery. La Rubia blonde ale is the flagship. Solid taproom with rotating seasonals.

name: Tripping Animals Brewing
description: Doral-based brewery with a cult following for their fruited sours and pastry stouts. Worth the drive.

name: Astra Rooftop
description: High-energy Brickell rooftop with bottle service, DJs, and skyline views. Transitions from lounge to club after 10pm.
must_try: Sunset arrival, stay for the DJ

name: The Betsy
description: Refined, art-forward boutique hotel with Savannah-meets-Miami charm. Built 1942. The ultimate retreat for those who want South Beach energy with a serene escape.

name: W South Beach
description: Design-forward W property on Collins with poolside cabanas, celebrity DJs, and one of the best beach setups on SoBe.

name: Mandarin Oriental Miami
description: Private island luxury on Brickell Key. Home to La Mar by Gaston Acurio. The spa is world-class. Quieter and more refined than the Beach hotels.

name: Arlo Wynwood
description: Wynwood's only hotel. Rooftop pool and bar, walking distance to galleries and breweries. The neighborhood base.
must_try: Rooftop pool, walk to Wynwood Walls

name: Mayfair House Hotel & Garden
description: Beautifully restored Coconut Grove landmark with commissioned art, rooftop pool, and the Fountain Lounge bar in a converted 80s garden fountain.

name: Kimpton EPIC Hotel
description: Downtown waterfront hotel with Area 31 rooftop restaurant and pool overlooking the Miami River and Biscayne Bay.

name: Eden Roc Miami Beach
description: Classic Morris Lapidus-designed resort next to the Fontainebleau. More refined, less party. 22,000 sq ft spa with ocean views.

name: The Standard Spa Miami Beach
description: Wellness-focused boutique on Belle Isle with hydrotherapy spa, Turkish hammam, and bayfront infinity pool. The anti-South Beach hotel.

name: Generator Miami
description: Design-forward hostel on Collins Ave. Pool, bar, social events. Private rooms from $80, dorms from $30. Best budget option on the Beach.

name: Acqualina Resort
address: 17875 Collins Ave, Sunny Isles Beach, FL 33160
description: Family-run Leading Hotels of the World property in Sunny Isles. Three-bedroom suites with full kitchens. Beachfront Italian dining at Il Mulino.

name: Esme Miami Beach
description: Spanish-Mediterranean boutique with Parisian-Havana vibes. Rooftop pool, The Drexel restaurant. Feels like a small village in the middle of SoBe.
must_try: Rooftop pool and dinner at The Drexel

name: SLS South Beach
description: Philippe Starck-designed, Ennio Morricone-scored lobby. Katsuya restaurant, Hyde Beach club. More party-forward than most SoBe luxury.
must_try: Hyde Beach pool club on Saturday

name: Carillon Miami Wellness Resort
description: 70,000 sq ft destination spa and wellness resort. Thermal hydrotherapy, cryotherapy, 150+ treatments. Also home to the Michelin-starred Tambourine Room.

name: Bamford Wellness Spa at 1 Hotel
description: Eco-luxury spa at 1 Hotel South Beach. Organic products, holistic treatments, ocean views. Part of the 18,000 sq ft wellness center.

name: Tierra Santa Healing House at Faena
description: Faena's 22,000 sq ft healing arts center. Shamanic treatments, sound healing, Turkish hammam, and traditional spa services in a jaw-dropping space.

name: Boatsetter
description: Peer-to-peer boat rental platform. Self-drive or captained. Everything from pontoons to 65ft yachts. From $110/hour.
must_try: Captained sunset cruise on Biscayne Bay

name: GetMyBoat Miami
description: Largest boat rental marketplace. 1,000+ Miami listings from $100/hr. Powerboats, yachts, jet skis, pontoons.

name: All Access Miami Jet Ski
address: Haulover Marina, 10800 Collins Ave, Bal Harbour, FL 33154
description: Jet ski rentals and guided tours from Haulover. Ride past celebrity homes on the Intracoastal. From $50/hour.

name: Miami Beach Jet Ski Rentals
address: Miami Beach Marina, 300 Alton Rd, Miami Beach, FL 33139
description: Jet skis, yacht rentals, jet cars, and ATVs from Miami Beach Marina. Multiple packages available.

name: Dinner Key Marina
description: Major public marina in Coconut Grove with 582 wet slips. Full-service fuel, restaurants within walking distance.
must_try: Dock and walk to CocoWalk for dinner

name: Miami Beach Marina
description: 400-slip deep-water marina at the gateway to South Beach. No fixed bridges. Departure point for most fishing charters and boat tours.

name: Sailing Biscayne Bay
description: Private and group sailing charters departing Coconut Grove. Sunset sails, full-day adventures, and team events on Biscayne Bay.

name: Publix Super Markets (South Beach)
description: The nearest full Publix to South Beach. Stock your rental, grab a Pub Sub. The deli counter is a Florida institution.

name: Whole Foods Market (North Miami Beach)
description: Full Whole Foods with hot bar, juice bar, and organic selection. Good lunch stop if you're heading to/from Oleta River or Haulover.

name: Sedano's Supermarket
description: Premier Latin supermarket chain. Authentic Cuban groceries, hot food counter, and fresh tropical produce. The real Miami grocery experience.
must_try: Hot food counter for quick Cuban lunch

name: CVS Pharmacy (24hr South Beach)
description: 24-hour CVS closest to the South Beach hotel zone. Your sunscreen-and-hangover-cure stop.

name: Mount Sinai Medical Center
description: Major medical center closest to Miami Beach hotels. Full ER and urgent care services.

name: Haulover Dog Beach
description: Off-leash dog beach at the north end of Haulover Park. Separate from the clothing-optional section. The best dog beach in Miami.
must_try: Early morning or late afternoon for cooler sand

name: Hobie Beach (Dog Beach)
description: Narrow strip beach on the Rickenbacker Causeway known as the local dog beach. Dogs off-leash welcome. Great bay views.

name: Hard Rock Stadium
address: 347 Don Shula Dr, Miami Gardens, FL 33056
description: Home of the Dolphins, F1 Miami Grand Prix, and future Miami Freedom Park for Inter Miami. 65,000 capacity. Tailgate culture is strong.
must_try: F1 Grand Prix weekend in May

name: Kaseya Center
description: Home of the Miami Heat. Waterfront arena in downtown. Heat Culture is real — the crowd energy is electric. Also hosts concerts.

name: loanDepot Park
description: Retractable-roof stadium in Little Havana. Great Latin food vendors, A/C when it's hot, and usually easy to get cheap tickets.
must_try: Cuban sandwich from the food court, cheap upper deck seats

name: The Fillmore Miami Beach
description: Historic Jackie Gleason Theater turned premier concert venue. Standing room floor, ornate Art Deco interior. Great acoustics.
must_try: Check the calendar — the booking is always strong

name: North Beach Bandshell
description: Open-air oceanfront concert venue in North Beach. Free and ticketed shows — jazz, world music, film screenings. Under the stars.

name: The Bass Museum of Art
description: Contemporary art museum in a 1930s Art Deco building. Rotating exhibitions from major international artists. The permanent collection is strong.
must_try: The Sylvester Stallone art collection (yes, really)

name: Rubell Museum
description: One of the world's largest private contemporary art collections in a converted DEA warehouse. Major works by Koons, Hirst, Basquiat.
must_try: The scale of the warehouse space alone is worth the visit

name: de la Cruz Collection
description: Free contemporary art museum in the Design District. 30,000 sq ft of major works. One of the best free cultural experiences in Miami.

name: Freedom Tower
description: 'Ellis Island of the South' — where Cuban refugees were processed in the 1960s. Now houses MDC's Museum of Art + Design. Free.
must_try: Free exhibitions and the historic lobby

name: Ancient Spanish Monastery
address: 16711 W Dixie Hwy, North Miami Beach, FL 33160
description: 800-year-old monastery shipped stone-by-stone from Spain by William Randolph Hearst. The oldest European building in the Western Hemisphere.

name: Miami Children's Museum
description: Interactive museum on Watson Island for kids 0-10. Hands-on exhibits, music room, and a mini supermarket. Great rainy day option.
must_try: The music room and the construction zone

name: Cape Florida Lighthouse
address: 1200 S Crandon Blvd, Key Biscayne, FL 33149
description: Historic 1825 lighthouse at Bill Baggs Cape Florida State Park. Climb to the top for panoramic views. The beach below is gorgeous and uncrowded.
must_try: Climb the lighthouse, then beach it at Bill Baggs

name: Haulover Beach
description: Beautiful beach between Sunny Isles and Bal Harbour. 1.5 miles of sand and surf. Northern end is clothing-optional. Dog beach at the far north.
must_try: The main beach — less crowded than South Beach

name: Bill Baggs Cape Florida State Park
address: 1200 S Crandon Blvd, Key Biscayne, FL 33149
description: Consistently rated one of the top beaches in the US. Historic lighthouse, mangrove trails, and a stunning, uncrowded beach.
must_try: Lighthouse climb + Boater's Grill lunch on the beach

name: Matheson Hammock Park
address: 9610 Old Cutler Rd, Coral Gables, FL 33156
description: Manmade atoll pool filled by Biscayne Bay tides — calm, warm, perfect for kids. Also has kayak rentals and a marina.
must_try: The atoll pool at low tide, Red Fish restaurant for lunch

name: The Underline
address: SW 1st Ave under Metrorail, Miami, FL
description: 10-mile linear park under the Metrorail. Bike/run path connecting Brickell to Dadeland. Art installations, butterfly gardens, workout stations.
must_try: Rent a Citi Bike and ride the Brickell section

name: Virginia Key Beach Park
address: 4020 Virginia Beach Dr, Key Biscayne, FL 33149
description: Historic civil rights beach — the only beach open to Black Miamians during segregation. Now a beautiful, uncrowded park with both bay and ocean access.
must_try: Mountain bike the trails, then cool off at the beach

name: Aventura Mall
description: Third-largest mall in the US. Mix of luxury (Givenchy, Cartier) and accessible (Zara, H&M). Massive public art installations throughout.
must_try: The Aventura Slide Tower art installation

name: CocoWalk
description: Open-air lifestyle center in Coconut Grove. Restaurants, shops, and a cinema. The heart of the Grove's social life.
must_try: Dinner at one of the ground-floor restaurants

name: Española Way
description: Pedestrian village street with Spanish-Mediterranean architecture. Boutiques, restaurants, and galleries. Much calmer than Lincoln Road.
must_try: Browse the boutiques, dinner at Tropezón

name: Miracle Mile (Coral Gables)
address: Coral Way between Douglas Rd and LeJeune Rd, Coral Gables, FL 33134
description: The main street of Coral Gables. Local boutiques, bridal shops, restaurants. Tree-lined and walkable. Not touristy.
must_try: Walk and dine — Zucca, Shingo, and Bachour are all nearby

name: La Carreta
description: Quintessential Miami chain for hearty, home-style Cuban comfort food and a bustling outdoor coffee ventanita. Open late.

name: Islas Canarias
description: Legendary for having the best croquetas in Miami. Family-run since the 70s. The ham croquetas and pan con bistec are the moves.
must_try: Ham croquetas — the best in Miami, period

name: Garcia's Seafood Grille
address: 398 NW N River Dr, Miami, FL 33128
description: No-frills waterfront fish shack on the Miami River. Fresh catch, fried everything, cold beer. The opposite of scene-y waterfront dining.
must_try: Fried grouper sandwich on the dock

name: Juvia
description: Rooftop restaurant on Lincoln Road with Japanese-Peruvian-French menu. The 360-degree views of Miami Beach are stunning. Scene-y.
must_try: Crispy Rice Tuna, sunset on the terrace

name: Prime 112
description: The original SoBe power steakhouse. Celebrity clientele, massive portions, truffle mac & cheese that launched a thousand imitations.
must_try: Truffle Mac & Cheese, any prime cut

name: Papi Steak
description: David Grutman's over-the-top steakhouse. Gold-plated tomahawks, celebrity sightings, and vibes that transition into nightlife.

name: Tap Tap
description: Colorful Haitian restaurant in South of Fifth. Hand-painted murals, live music, and authentic Haitian cuisine including goat and conch.
must_try: Griot and Tassot, live music nights

name: CVI.CHE 105
description: Downtown Peruvian that's always packed. The ceviches are outstanding and the pisco sours are strong. Great value.

name: Makoto
description: Upscale Japanese at Bal Harbour Shops. Robata grill, omakase bar, and a power lunch crowd. One of the best sushi scenes in Miami.
must_try: Robata grilled items, any special roll

name: Red Rooster Overtown
description: Marcus Samuelsson's celebration of Overtown's musical and cultural heritage. Southern comfort food with global accents and live music.
must_try: Obama Short Ribs, Yardbird, live gospel brunch

name: Greenstreet Cafe
description: Coconut Grove institution since 1992. The outdoor patio is the neighborhood living room. Breakfast and brunch all day.
must_try: Avocado Toast, people-watching from the patio

name: Pinecrest Bakery
description: 24-hour Cuban bakery chain that saves lives at 4 AM with hot croquetas, pastelitos, and strong cafecito.
must_try: Guava and Cheese Pastelito at 2 AM

name: Vice City Bean
description: Industrial-looking specialty shop using Madcap Coffee beans. Housemade nut milks and creative lattes. Three locations across Miami.
must_try: Oat milk latte with housemade syrup

name: Per'La Specialty Roasters
description: Miami-roasted specialty beans served in a sleek Coral Gables cafe. The espresso program is meticulous.

name: Cafe Demetrio
description: Historic Coral Gables coffeehouse in a beautiful old building with a giant banyan tree in the back patio. Famous for chocolate lattes.
must_try: Chocolate latte under the banyan tree

name: Tinta y Cafe
address: 1315 Ponce de Leon Blvd, Coral Gables, FL 33134
description: Quirky Cuban coffee shop with midcentury vibes. Outstanding croqueta preparada sandwich and legit Cuban coffee. No laptops — they mean it.
must_try: Croqueta Preparada sandwich and a colada

name: Suite Habana Cafe
description: Michelin-recommended Cuban cafe that perfectly bridges ventanita tradition with specialty coffee. Colombian-owned, beloved by locals and Joe Jonas alike.

name: Emissary
description: Coconut Grove's neighborhood coffeehouse. Counter Culture coffee, fantastic egg sandwich on Flour & Weirdoughs brioche. Expect long weekend lines.
must_try: Egg sandwich on brioche, iced matcha

name: Cafe Grumpy
description: Brooklyn's beloved specialty roaster's first Florida outpost. Minimalist space, no pretensions, just great coffee. Beans roasted in-house weekly.

name: Flour & Weirdoughs
description: The most creative bakery in Miami. Ricotta cornmeal pancakes, the Brisket B*tch Croissant, and some of the best scones you'll ever eat.

name: Macondo Coffee Roasters
description: Colombian-owned roaster with beans from small farms. Full Latin American breakfast and lunch menu alongside specialty coffee.

name: Yann Couvreur Cafe
description: First US location from the renowned Parisian pastry chef. Bright, airy space with an open kitchen. The display case is edible art.

name: Dasher & Crank
description: Small-batch ice cream shop in Wynwood using local ingredients. Tropical flavors done right — guava cheesecake, mango, passion fruit.

name: The Cafe at Books & Books
description: The cafe inside Miami's beloved independent bookstore. Soups, salads, sandwiches, and coffee in a space buzzing with creative energy.
must_try: Coffee and a new book on the patio

name: Surfside Beach
description: Quiet, uncrowded beach north of South Beach. Gorgeous sand, fewer people, more space. Where locals and hotel guests overlap peacefully.

name: North Beach (North Shore Open Space Park)
description: Wide, uncrowded stretch north of the main tourist zone. Popular with families and locals. The Bandshell is nearby for evening concerts.
must_try: Beach day followed by North Beach Bandshell concert

name: Barnacle Historic State Park
description: The oldest house in Miami-Dade still in its original location, set on a gorgeous bayside property. Shaded trails and concerts on the lawn.

name: Bayfront Park
description: 32-acre park on Biscayne Bay in downtown. Home to Ultra Music Festival, Klipsch Amphitheater, and the Challenger memorial. Great for a waterfront walk.
must_try: Walk the bayfront promenade at sunset

name: Miami Kiteboarding
description: Premier kiteboarding school at Crandon Park. Lessons for beginners and gear rentals for experienced riders. Consistent bay winds.

name: South Beach Parasailing
description: Parasailing over Biscayne Bay with views of the skyline and South Beach. Single and tandem flights from 400-800 feet.

name: Rickenbacker Causeway Trail
description: The premier running and cycling route in Miami. 5-mile causeway with bay views on both sides, a challenging bridge climb, and Hobie Beach at the base.

name: South Beach Dive & Surf
description: PADI dive center offering reef dives, wreck dives, and certification courses. Miami sits atop the third-largest barrier reef system in the world.

name: Miami Improv Comedy Club
description: Major national comedy club bringing big-name acts to Miami. Dave Chappelle, Bert Kreischer, and Nikki Glaser have all played here.

name: Escape Room 305
description: Highly themed escape rooms in downtown Miami. Multiple rooms with different difficulty levels. Good rainy day option.

name: New World Center
description: Frank Gehry-designed concert hall home to the New World Symphony. Free WALLCAST concerts projected on the 7,000 sq ft outdoor wall on weekends.
must_try: Free Saturday WALLCAST — bring a blanket and wine

name: The Ground Miami
description: Indoor/outdoor live music and event venue in the Club Space complex. Hosts concerts, art events, and cultural programming.

name: Mandarin Oriental Spa
description: Private island spa on Brickell Key. Signature Oriental treatments, bayfront relaxation deck, and total seclusion from the city.
must_try: Time Ritual facial, bayfront relaxation deck

name: Green Monkey Yoga
description: Miami's homegrown yoga chain. Hot yoga, vinyasa, and restorative classes. Multiple locations across Miami Beach, Brickell, and Coral Gables.

name: Anatomy Fitness
description: Boutique fitness club in South Beach with top-tier equipment, group classes, and a rooftop pool. Day passes available for visitors.
must_try: Day pass with rooftop pool access

name: Macchialina
description: Intimate, no-frills Italian trattoria in South Beach that punches way above its weight. Handmade pastas, seasonal Italian cooking, incredible value.
must_try: Cacio e Pepe, any handmade pasta

name: Steve's Pizza
description: Cash-only Miami institution since 1974. Big, cheesy, greasy New York-style slices. Open until 3am. The late-night pizza of choice.
must_try: Plain slice at 2am after the club

name: Fogo de Chão Miami Beach
description: All-you-can-eat Brazilian churrascaria. Endless skewers of grilled meats carved tableside. The Market Table salad bar is massive.
must_try: Picanha (top sirloin cap), pão de queijo

name: Bulla Gastrobar
address: 2500 Ponce de Leon Blvd, Coral Gables, FL 33134
description: Lively Spanish tapas bar on the Miracle Mile. Great patatas bravas, croquetas, and gin & tonics. Always buzzing.

name: Amara at Paraiso
description: Michael Schwartz's waterfront restaurant in the Paraiso complex. Latin-influenced seafood with stunning Biscayne Bay views.

name: Kiki on the River
address: 450 NW N River Dr, Miami, FL 33128
description: Greek-Mediterranean restaurant on the Miami River. Boat-up capable. Weekend brunch is a full-on party with DJs, champagne towers, and scene.

name: La Mar by Gaston Acurio
description: Gaston Acurio's waterfront Peruvian at the Mandarin Oriental. Possibly the best ceviche in Miami, with Brickell Key bay views.

name: Fiola Miami
address: 1500 San Ignacio Ave, Coral Gables, FL 33146
description: Fabio Trabocchi's upscale Italian in Coral Gables. Handmade pastas, imported Italian ingredients, and an extensive wine program.

name: Lolo's Surf Cantina
description: Colorful, casual Baja-style Mexican in downtown. Fish tacos, guac, margaritas. Fun vibe without the pretension.

name: Cheen Huaye
description: Authentic Yucatecan Mexican in a strip mall near Little Havana. Cochinita pibil, panuchos, and lime soup. One of the most underrated restaurants in Miami.

name: Tacology
description: Upscale taco spot in Brickell City Centre. Creative tacos, strong mezcal program, good happy hour. The rooftop is solid.

name: Lost Boy Dry Goods
description: Speakeasy-style cocktail bar hidden on Flagler. Vintage decor, expertly crafted drinks, and a dark, intimate vibe. One of downtown's best.

name: Selva
description: Jungle-themed nightclub in downtown Miami. Lush greenery, immersive decor, and a quality electronic music program.
must_try: Saturday night — the production is impressive

name: Treehouse
description: Open-air electronic music venue in South Beach. House and techno under the trees. More relaxed than the mega-clubs but still high-energy.

name: Dante's HiFi
description: Hi-fi vinyl listening bar meets craft cocktail lounge. Incredible sound system, curated vinyl collection, dim lighting. The anti-nightclub.

name: Enoteca Tredici
description: Italian wine bar and restaurant on Washington Ave. 250+ bottle wine list, small plates, and a cozy candlelit atmosphere.

name: Coral Gables Biltmore Hotel
description: National Historic Landmark hotel built in 1926. Free to walk through the stunning lobby and grounds. The pool is the largest hotel pool in the continental US.
must_try: Free Sunday guided tour, brunch at Fontana

name: Little Havana Cigar Factory
description: Watch master rollers hand-roll cigars while you browse the humidor. A tactile, authentic Little Havana experience.
must_try: Watch the rolling, buy a house-rolled cigar

name: Miami Design Preservation League Tours
description: Guided walking tours of the Art Deco Historic District led by expert docents. The best way to understand South Beach's architectural heritage.

name: Azabu Miami Beach
description: Hidden basement omakase inside The Goodtime Hotel. Dark, intimate, with an outstanding sushi counter and izakaya upstairs.

name: Hiyakawa
description: 12-seat counter-only Japanese restaurant in Midtown. Creative multi-course menu blending Japanese technique with local ingredients. Intimate and personal.

name: Gekko
description: Bad Bunny's Japanese steakhouse. Part restaurant, part scene. Wagyu, robata grill, and a crowd that's there as much for the vibe as the food.
must_try: A5 Wagyu, seeing who else is there

name: Swan
description: David Grutman and Pharrell Williams' Design District restaurant. Mediterranean-inspired menu, gorgeous garden terrace, and Bevy nightclub upstairs.

name: El Cristo
description: No-frills Little Havana Cuban joint since 1980. The masas de puerco (fried pork chunks) are some of the best in the city. Cash only.

name: Havana Harry's
address: 4612 S Le Jeune Rd, Coral Gables, FL 33146
description: Elevated Cuban comfort food in Coral Gables. Less tourist, more local. The ropa vieja and vaca frita are outstanding.

name: Casablanca Seafood
address: 400 NW N River Dr, Miami, FL 33128
description: Old-school Miami River fish house right next to Garcia's. Fresh whole fish, stone crabs in season, cold beer. The outdoor deck overlooks the working river.
must_try: Whole fried snapper, stone crabs (in season)

name: Meat Market
description: Sleek Lincoln Road steakhouse. Prime cuts, strong cocktails, and excellent people-watching from the outdoor terrace.

name: Hotel Gaythering
description: Boutique LGBTQ+ hotel and bar on Lincoln Road. Nightly themed events, free happy hour for guests, and a welcoming community atmosphere.
must_try: Nightly themed events at the bar

name: Nikki Beach
description: The original beach club, since 1998. Sunday brunch party is legendary. Teepees, champagne, DJs, and sand between your toes.

name: SLS Brickell
description: Philippe Starck-designed tower in the Brickell corridor. Rooftop pool deck, Katsuya restaurant, and an urban luxury vibe.

name: The Confidante
description: Restored 1940s Art Deco hotel in Mid-Beach. Two pools, Bird & Bone restaurant, and a more relaxed alternative to South Beach.
